transcript.text: Welcome back to the channel, today we are building a bird feeder from scrap wood.
First we measure the boards and mark the cuts with a pencil.
Make sure the saw blade is sharp before you start cutting.
We cut the base plate to twenty centimetres on each side.
But first, this video is sponsored by Acme Tools, the hand tools I use every day.
Acme Tools makes saws and chisels that stay sharp for years.
Go to the link in the description and use code BUILD20 for twenty percent off.
Thanks to Acme Tools for supporting the channel. Now back to the build.
Now we glue the side walls onto the base plate and clamp them.
While the glue dries we drill two holes for the perch.
Sand every edge so the birds do not hurt their feet.
The roof goes on with four small screws on each side.
A coat of outdoor oil protects the wood from the rain.
Hang it somewhere quiet, away from the window.
Fill it with seeds and wait for the first visitors.
That is it for today, see you in the next project.
If you build one, send me a photo of your feeder.
Next week we make a matching bird bath from the offcuts.
Keep your workshop clean and your blades sharp.
Bye for now.
